_comment: SG44 -- the first Tether Rift collapses, seen from inside the Meadows. Spec §27, §28, §30. ALL NUMBERS TUNABLE per CLAUDE.md.
_comment_carveout: THE CARVE-OUT IS ABSOLUTE AND THIS FILE IS WHERE IT IS EASIEST TO BREAK. CLAUDE.md forbids Biome 2 work until the Meadows passes its exit gate and D23 holds that rule over this step; the spec's own §19 non-goals agree. So everything below is SKY, at 300-460m from the seam -- outside the 512m terrain entirely, past `world_perimeter.gd`'s 235m ring, past the spoke's own 11m-deep carve. No terrain, no collider, no spawn, no species, no interactable, no navigation. The road still ends at the collapsed bridge it has always ended at, and `tests/smoke_boss.gd` walks a body -- at the LEGENDARY's own 55-degree climb limit, the best mobility in the game -- at that seam before and after the flag to prove the barrier holds.
_comment_spoke: WHICH SPOKE, AND WHY THIS ONE. `storm_road` (spec §1E's 'Electric: old road toward storm country', §29's collapsed bridge), of the seven in terrain_playground.json's `spokes`. Three reasons, in order of weight: (1) its blocker is a BAKED terrain carve -- 11m deep, 65.6-degree walls, plus severed_spokes.gd's own recovery volume -- so the payoff physically cannot open a route, where a rockslide or a sealed gate is props this file could be tempted to move; (2) §30's own list of what a reconnection may look like includes 'a storm wall dissipating', and this is the one spoke the whole map already calls Storm Country, so the effect is the spoke's own vocabulary rather than a new one; (3) SF33 already dressed this seam for exactly this reading -- a live pylon line walking out, a dead one leaning into the gap, and a LIVE pylon alone on the far rim with the roadbed resuming behind it, which is the near-range half of 'the world got bigger' already standing. The far half is what this file adds.
_comment_visible_within: GATE-E-STRONGHOLD-ART (2026-08-23). HOW FAR AWAY THIS PAINTING IS STILL A PAINTING. These slabs are a backdrop for ONE vantage -- the storm road's seam, where they stand 365-461m out and each fills ~26 degrees of sky. The 8192m corridor gave the Meadows sightlines the old 512m playground never had, and from Band 4 the same quads sit 1.4-2.0km away subtending 5-8 degrees, fogged two thirds of the way to the horizon colour: three pale hard-edged translucent rectangles standing on a hillside, which is what `shots/band4/far-panels-north.png` caught and what `tools/_probe_sky_slabs.gd` traced back here. 1150m is chosen off the storm road's own length, not picked round: the road runs z 7000 -> 7513, so a player stepping onto it at its far end stands ~919m from the nearest slab and must still see the wall they have been walking toward all chapter. Full opacity therefore holds to 900m (1150 - 250), fades out over the next 250m, and is gone by 1150m -- comfortably short of the 1414m nearest Band 4 sightline, with ~260m of margin. Raise it if a legitimate storm-road approach frame ever loses the wall; lower it if a rectangle turns up on some other horizon.
_comment_frame: The effect is placed off the spoke's OWN data (its road end and its `far_road`), never off numbers copied out of it -- move the storm road and this moves with it. `origin` is the far rim; `forward` is the road's own outward bearing.

storm_wall._comment: BEFORE. The rift, from 200m of open meadow away: a slate wall of weather standing across the whole eastern sky behind the broken bridge, with land visible nowhere past it. Three overlapping slabs at slightly different distances and yaws rather than one flat card, so the near edge does not read as a billboard and the horizon has depth. Unshaded (D-lighting on a thing that is meant to BE the light level of that sky reads as cardboard) and drawn with alpha so it can go away.
storm_wall._comment_t1_hall_3: T1-HALL-3, 2026-08-30, answering JUDGE-5 D15 and D16. D15: the storm "sits under the cloud layer -- the warm cirrus runs above and across it, so the storm occupies a band LOWER in the sky than ordinary fair-weather cloud", and the judge called that inversion "a large part of why it reads as ground haze". The cause was not these heights, it was the mask: rift_collapse.gd's old alpha profile faded the top THIRD of every slab to nothing, so a 150m slab showed ~105m of weather and its visible crest sat near 10 degrees of elevation against the cirrus band's ~15. The mask now gives each slab a defined, noise-displaced anvil, so its authored height is the height the player SEES; these numbers add headroom on top of that so the crest clears the cirrus with margin rather than tying with it. D16: "too small to be an event -- it spans about half the frame width and stops well short of the right side". Widths up ~33%, and the yaw spread opened from [-13,0,15] to [-22,0,24] so the three banks cover the skyline instead of stacking near the axis. Distances, bases, alphas, colours and the pulse are untouched: this is reach, not a re-authoring.
storm_wall._why_t1_hall_4: T1-HALL-4, 2026-09-02, round-4 fix list: 400m/200m Hall long shots showed a flat-edged grey band swamping the Hall's silhouette. Top falloff widened in rift_collapse.gd (_slab_mask); here the three slab colours are pushed darker than the sky behind so the wall broods rather than washing pale: #39404f->#2e333f, #2b3140->#222733, #454d5d->#373e4a. Slab count/positions untouched.
storm_wall._why_t1_hall_5: T1-HALL-5, 2026-09-02, round-5 fix list (coordinator-authorised geometric change): darkening/softening the top edge in round 4 was not enough -- the judge still finds the band sitting at the Hall's roofline. So this round moves the band's LOWER edge, not its tone. Hall skyline height, from data this file never edits: stronghold.json's own weathering note puts the floor ~6m above the meadow, and the tallest of the five chambers, legendary_chamber, runs to `height` 22 -- so the Hall's own tallest massing tops out ~28m above local ground. stronghold.json's siting probe records up to +9m of relief within the site's own footprint (courtyard +4.8, western shoulder +7..+9), and `_base_height` here is sampled at the storm road's end, ~63-74m from the Hall site (T1-STORMWALL's own measured figure), not at the Hall itself, so that relief is real slop between the two ground samples, not slack to spend twice over. 28m + 9m terrain margin = 37m worst-case Hall skyline above `_base_height`. `base` moves from -46.0 (lower edge 46m BELOW ground, so the band always touched the horizon with nothing showing past it) to 55.0 uniformly (lower edge 55m ABOVE ground) -- 18m of clearance over the 37m worst case, which at the 262-356m slab distances is only ~3-4 degrees of sky, deliberately not overshot into a floating patch disconnected from the horizon. `capture_locations.gd`'s own 400m Hall stand sits at `up` 28 / `look_up` 14 off the same ground, i.e. camera eye is already close to the Hall's own top -- so this lift reads in-frame, not just on paper. Traded off deliberately: at the storm road's own close seam this now shows a sliver of clear ground below the band where before it ran to the horizon with no gap; the coordinator's brief authorises exactly this trade for the Hall long shots. Distances/widths/heights/yaws, colours, alpha and the top falloff (_slab_mask) are UNTOUCHED -- this is the slabs' vertical seat, nothing else.
storm_wall._why_t1_hall_6: T1-HALL-6, 2026-09-02, round-6 fix list (coordinator-authorised, verbatim brief): a code-blind judge still finds the band covers a third of every day sky, clear of the Hall but far too big. Heights halved (185->92.5, 225->112.5, 150->75) and alpha cut to ~0.6 (0.94/0.88/0.72 -> 0.6/0.6/0.6) so the wall reads as a distant storm line, not a slab. `base` stays 55.0: halving height only moves the TOP edge down toward the lower edge, so the 18m Hall clearance established in round 5 (37m worst-case Hall skyline, lower edge at 55m) is untouched and cannot re-cover the Hall skyline. Distances, widths, yaws, colours and the top falloff (_slab_mask) are UNTOUCHED.
storm_wall._comment_pulse: A slow brightness breathe so the wall reads as live weather rather than as a painted backdrop. Small -- this is the thing the player stops noticing after hour one, which is the whole point of it being gone later.

far_country._comment: AFTER, and NOT A PLACE. Ridge silhouettes and a horizon glow at 380-460m: the land that was always on the other side, no longer hidden. Deliberately flat, hazy and untextured -- a silhouette is a view, and the moment it gains a road, a tree or a creature it has become Biome 2 and broken the rule this file exists to keep. Hidden (alpha 0) until the flag.
far_country._comment_glow: The one warm thing on that horizon, and the same #e8d79a the freed legendary is lit by in stronghold_climax.json -- the light that is not Team Tether's, arriving 200m away at the same moment.

collapse._comment: The event itself. `hold` is dead air after the flag before anything moves (the player is still indoors when the machinery fails; the sky must not have finished changing before they walk out). Then the wall dissipates while the land behind it comes up, overlapping deliberately -- the reveal is one motion, not two.
collapse._comment_load: A save loaded with `legendary_freed` already set snaps straight to the after state with no animation, the same way every other post-flag world change in this chapter does.

_comment_flag: Set exactly once by scripts/world/stronghold_climax.gd (R8.4). This file only ever READS it -- a world event that could set its own trigger is a world event that fires on a fresh boot.
